content.text:
Sorry, you're right: I broke the ribbon's tabs, and they're back now. To fix the double border between the project name and the first tab, I set a one-pixel negative margin on each tab. Any style set on a gpui-kit `Tab` stops it being drawn, so the whole tab row went blank. No test caught it, because the ribbon tests call the tab click handler and look for command buttons directly, never checking that tabs are drawn.

**The fix** (`src/ribbon/mod.rs`)
- **Separate bars:** each ribbon tab is now its own single-tab bar in a plain row, the way the chat input's tabs already work. A plain container can take a style where a `Tab` can't.
- **Overlap only open tabs:** an open tab shifts one pixel left, so its border lands on the line before it (the project name's divider or a neighbouring open tab). A closed tab stays put, so it never covers a line.
- **Bottom line:** the project name area and the space before the collapse button draw it.

**How I checked it:** I had no way to see the window before, so I added a test helper (`src/frame_image.rs`). It draws a test frame's shapes into an image, without text or icons. I looked at the ribbon in both modes with Project and Code open, then Research after a closed Spec. Every line in the tab row is single, and none is hidden.

**New test** (`ribbon_tabs_are_drawn_beside_the_project_indicator`):
- **What it checks:** in dark and light mode, a selected Project tab is drawn right at the project name's divider, and nothing in the tab row doubles a line.
- **Proof it works:** I put the broken margin back and confirmed the test fails.

All 190 tests pass (1 ignored), the release build has no warnings, and `piton check` and `piton build check` pass. I haven't opened the app to look; rebuild and launch to confirm it looks right to you.
